operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11486 (signed 1969-10-03, 34 FR 15527) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after board has made its report"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 24606 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11486 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".

TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the  
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A  attached  
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Employes’ Conference Committee composed of labor  
organizations designated in List B attached hereto and made a part  
hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to  
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation  
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily  
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or  
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the  
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or  
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

First and whole-order end: express revocation by EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25, effective on signing; no effective-date wording), table row quoted in the clause reason. The dossier listed 'target provision not located: EO:12553'; I located the operative sentence and the table row in the held EO 12553 text and quote them exactly; no machine ACT record exists for this pair, and the claim cites the whole held EO 12553 text as its source. Status NO (provisional) is consistent. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11492 (signed 1969-10-30, 34 FR 17721) amends Sec. 3(a) of EO 11398 by substituting a new subsection that establishes the Citizens Advisory Committee on Physical Fitness and Sports; its only command is that substitution, and it has no own-terms end. First end: EO 11562 (signed 1970-09-25, 35 FR 15063), whose Sec. 7 reads "S ec. 7. Revocations." and, on the following lines, "and Executive Order No. 11492 of October 30,1969, are hereby revoked." (the sentence names EO 11398 and EO 11492 by number). EO 11562 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1970-09-25 (the FR filing date, 1970-09-28, is not used). The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 11562, September 25, 1970". The amended parent EO 11398 is revoked by the same sentence, so the amendment and its parent end on the same date. Sec. 6 of EO 11562 continues the Committee's function under the new Council: see the savings entry.

THE PRESIDENT 15063
Executive Order 11562
DEVELOPING AND COORDINATING A NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR  
PHYSICAL FITNESS AND SPORTS
By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States, it is hereby ordered as follows :
S ection  1. Program  fo r 'physical fitness and sports. The Secretary 
of Health, Education, and Welfare (hereinafter referred to as “the 
Secretary”) shall, in carrying out his responsibilities in relation to 
education and public health, including specifically the health of 
children and youth, develop and coordinate a national program for 
physical fitness and sports. The Secretary shall :
(1) Enlist the active support and assistance of individual citizens, 
civic groups, professional associations, amateur and professional sports 
groups, private enterprise, voluntary organizations, and others in 
efforts to promote and improve physical fitness and sports participation 
programs for all Americans;
(2) Stimulate, improve, and strengthen coordination of Federal 
services and programs relating to physical fitness and sports 
participation ;
(3) Encourage State and local governments in efforts to enhance 
physical fitness and sports participation;
(4) Seek to strengthen the physical fitness of American children, 
youth, and adults by systematically encouraging the development of 
community centered and other physical fitness and sports participation 
programs to encourage innovation, improve teacher preparation, and 
strengthen State and local leadership;
(5) Develop cooperative programs with medical, dental, and other 
similar professional societies to encourage and implement sound 
physical fitness practices;
(6) Stimulate and encourage research in the areas of physical 
fitness and sports performance ; and
(7) Improve school health and physical education programs for 
all pupils, including the handicapped and the physically under­
developed, by assisting educational agencies in developing quality 
programs to encourage innovation, improve teacher preparation, and 
strengthen State and local leadership.
S ec. 2. President's Cov/ncil on P hysical Fitness and Sports,  (a) 
There is hereby established the President’ s Council on Physical Fitness 
and Sports (hereinafter referred to as “the Council”), which shall 
be composed of the President’ s Consultant on Physical Fitness, who 
shall be the Chairman, and fourteen other members appointed by the 
President. The Council shall meet on the call of the Chairman.
(b) The members of the Council shall receive no compensation from 
the United States by reason of their service on the Council, but shall 
be reimbursed for travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of sub­
sistence, as authorized by law for persons serving the Government 
without compensation (5 U.S.C. 5703).
S ec. 3. Functions o f the Cov/ncil. (a) The Council shall advise the 
President and the Secretary concerning progress made in carrying out 
the provisions of this order and shall recommend to the President and 
the Secretary, as necessary, steps to accelerate progress.
(b) The Council shall advise the Secretary on matters pertaining 
to ways and means of enhancing opportunities for participation in 
physical fitness and sports activities and on State, local, and private 
action to extend and improve physical activity programs and 
services.
FEDERAL REGISTER, VOL. 35, NO. 189— TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 29, 1970

S eo. 4. Conference on ’ P hysical Fitness and Sports,  (a) There is  
hereby established a Conference on Physical Fitness and Sports 
(hereinafter referred to as “the Conference”) , which shall be composed 
of one hundred members whom the President may from time to time 
appoint. The Conference shall meet on the call of the Secretary to 
assist him in carrying out his responsibilities under this order.
(b) The members of the Conference shall receive no compensation 
or expense allowances from the United States Government by rea­
son of their service on the Conference.
S ec. 5. Assistance by Agencies,  (a) The Secretary and the Coun­
cil are authorized to request from any Federal department or agency 
information or assistance deemed necessary to carry out their func­
tions under this order, and each department and agency is authorized, 
to the extent permitted by law and within the limits of available funds, 
to furnish such information and assistance to the Secretary and the 
Council.
(b) The Secretary shall appoint the Executive Director of the 
Council. Subject to law, (1) the Department of Health, Education, 
and Welfare shall furnish necessary staff, supplies, facilities, and 
other administrative services for the Council, (2) expenses of the 
Council shall be met from funds available to the Secretary, and (3) 
the Department may provide staff assistance to the Conference.
S ec. 6. C ontinuity, (a) The Council established by this order shall 
be deemed to be a continuation of the Citizens Advisory Committee 
on Physical Fitness and Sports which has heretofore existed under 
Executive Order No. 11398 of March 4,1968, as amended.
(b) The seal prescribed by Executive Order No. 10830 of July 24, 
1959, as amended, shall be the seal of the President’s Council on 
Physical Fitness and Sports as reconstituted herein.
S ec. 7. Revocations.  Executive Order No. 11398 of March 4, 1968, 
and Executive Order No. 11492 of October 30,1969, are hereby revoked.
S ec. 8. Construction.  Nothing in this order shall be construed to 
abrogate, modify, or restrict any function vested by law in, or assigned 
pursuant to law to, any Federal department or agency or any officer 
thereof.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11543 (signed 1970-07-07, 35 FR 11009) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 24863 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11543 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".

Executive Order 11543
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes exist between th§ carriers represented by the 
National Eailway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the United Transportation Union, a labor organization; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore- been adjusted 
under the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten Substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, 
to investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway. Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes 
arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11547 (signed 1970-07-10, 35 FR 11221) amends Sec. 101(a) of EO 11330 (President's Council on Youth Opportunity) by substituting a new subsection establishing the Council and setting its membership; its only command is that substitution and it has no own-terms end. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose Sec. 17 reads "Sec. 17. Executive Order No. 11330, as amended, establishing the President’s" and, on the next line, "Council on Youth Opportunity, is revoked." EO 12379 does not name EO 11547 by number; it revokes EO 11330 'as amended', and because EO 11547's whole operative content is the substituted Sec. 101(a) of EO 11330, the revocation of EO 11330 as amended removes the section it amends and ends the clause. EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". The dossier's second chain event, dated 1975-01-06 (EO 11829), comes from a source-ladder file filed under EO 11829 that is a reprint of the 47 FR 36099 pages of EO 12379, not an event of 1975. Disclosed alternative reading: if a reviewer holds that an order not named by number is not ended by the revocation of its amended parent, no first end is shown in the held sources.

By virtue of the authority vested in me as President of the United 
States, Executive Order No. 113301  of March 5,1967, “Providing for 
the Coordination of Youth Opportunity Programs,” is hereby 
amended by substituting the following for Section 101 (a) :
“S ection  101. Membership and chairmanship, (a) There is hereby 
established the President’s Council on Youth Opportunity (herein­
after referred to as the “Council”). The Council shall be composed of 
the Vice President, who shall serve as Chairman, the Secretary of 
State, the Secretary of Defense, the Attorney General, the Post­
master General, the Secretary of the Interior, the Secretary of Agri­
culture, the. Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of Labor, the 
Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare, the Secretary of Hous­
ing and Urban Development, the Secretary of Transportation, the 
Director of the Office of Economic Opportunity, the Chairman of the 
Civil Service Commission, and such other Federal officials as the 
President may designate. Each of the foregoing may appoint a 
delegate to represent him in Council affairs.”

research_rationale:
EO 11547 (signed 1970-07-10, 35 FR 11221) read in full from the held official FR text, with the relevant parts of EO 11330 and EO 12379. Identity confirmed. The order is a single amendment (substituted Sec. 101(a) of EO 11330). First and whole-order end: EO 12379 Sec. 17 revoking EO 11330 'as amended' (1982-08-17, on signing), reasoned as removal of the section amended; EO 11547 is not named by number, which is stated in the clause reason with the alternative reading. The dossier listed 'target provision not located: EO:12379'; I located Sec. 17 and quote it. A Cruden by-number scan of EO 11330 found only EO 11547 and EO 12379 (and mirrors/reprints) citing it. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.

No later amendment of EO 11547's text is held.","independent_command_check":"No independent command: the substituted subsection operates only inside EO 11330 and has no standing apart from it.","savings_check":"No savings or residual effect is shown: EO 12379 has no savings wording and no held text transfers the Council's functions.","scope_check":"The order has one operative paragraph (the substitution of Sec. 101(a)), so the single whole-order clause ends on one date."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11558 (signed 1970-09-18, 35 FR 14683) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 25027 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11558 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11558
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the United Transportation Union, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of five members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

THE PRESIDENT 14683
Executive Order 11558
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the United Transportation Union, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of five members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.
T he  W h ite H ouse,

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11559 (signed 1970-09-18, 35 FR 14687) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 25100 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11559 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".

Executive Order 11559
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the three labor organizations, designated in List B attached 
hereto and made a part hereof; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Jict, as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board of five members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

spread of the disease. The restrictions  
pertaining to the interstate movement  
of swine and swine products from or  
through quarantined areas as contained  
in 9 CFR Part 76, as amended, will apply  
to the quarantined portions of such  
counties.
The amendments impose certain fur­
ther restrictions necessary to prevent the  
interstate spread of hog cholera and  
must be made effective immediately to  
accomplish their purpose in the public  
interest. Accordingly, under the adminis­
trative procedure provisions in 5 U.S.C.  
553, it is found upon good cause that  
notice and other public procedure with  
respect to the amendments are imprac­
ticable and contrary to the public inter­
est, and good cause is found for making  
them effective less than 30 days after  
publication in the F ederal R egister.
Done at Washington, D.C., this 17th  
day of September 1970.

PART 39— AIRWORTHINESS 
DIRECTIVES
AiResearch Model TPE331—  1  and — 2 
Series Engines High Speed Pinion  
Bearing
A recent failure of a bearing on the  
high-speed pinion shaft in a Model TPE  
331-1 engine resulted in a failure of the  
engine. A number of these bearings have  
shown excessive wear within a few hours  
of operation during production runs of  
new engines. Impending failure of the  
bearing due to premature wear can be  
detected by analysis of an engine oil sam­
ple and inspection of the oil filter for  
metal particles. A partial failure of the  
bearing and high-speed pinion may be  
indicated by fluctuation or loss of engine  
torque pressure.
RULES AND REGULATIONS
Since this condition is likely to exist or  
develop in engines of this type design in  
service, an airworthiness directive is be­
ing issued to require an engine oil sam­
ple analysis and visual inspection of the  
oil filter. In addition, a revision to the  
airplane flight manuals is required to ad­
vise the pilot to shut down the engine if  
torque fluctuation or loss of torque pres­
sure occurs.
Since a situation exists that requires  
immediate adoption of this regulation, it  
is found that notice and public procedure  
hereon are impracticable and good cause  
exists for making this amendment effec­
tive in less than 30 days.
In consideration of the foregoing, and  
pursuant to the authority delegated to  
me by the Administrator (31 F.R. 13697),  
§  39.13 of Part 39 of the Federal Aviation 
Regulations is amended by adding the  
following new Airworthiness Directive:
AiResearch . The AiResearch Manufacturing  
Co. of Arizona. Applies to Turbopropeller  
Engines Model TPE331-1 and -2 installed  
in, but not limited to Mooney MU-2,  
AJerlin 2B, Volpar Turboliner, and Short  
Skyvan Aircraft.
Compliance required as indicated.
To detect impending failure of the high­
speed pinion bearings accomplish the fol­
lowing :
(a) New engines with less than 25 hours’  
time in service or overhauled engines with  
less than 25 hours’  time in service since over­
haul on the effective date of thiá AD must  
have the following accomplished:
(1) After more than 5 hours’  time in serv­
ice, but before exceeding 25 hours’  time in  
service after the effective date of this AD,  
an engine oil samplé and the engine oil  
filter element must be returned to AiResearch  
Manufacturing Co., or a facility approved' by  
the Chief, Aircraft Engineering Division, FA A,  
Western Region, for laboratory examination.
(2) Prior to operation of the engine in ex­
cess of 35 hours’  time in service, either since  
new or since time of overhaul, the owner or  
operator must recieve written confirmation  
from AiResearch, or other approved facility,  
that an acceptable level of oil contamination  
exists.
(3) The provisions of (a) (1) and (2),  
above, must be complied with after each  
subsequent overhaul unless the engine log  
book indicates that the engine wa3 subjected  
to a 5-hour acceptance test as described in  
the FAA-approved overhaul procedures as re­
vised September 1, 1970, and a determination  
of acceptable oil and filter contamination  
was made by AiResearch or other FAA-  
approved facility prior to returning the  
engine to service.
(b) A one time inspection of new engines  
with more than 25 hours but less than 50  
hours’  time in service or overhauled engines  
with more than 25 hours’  time in service but  
less than 50 hours’  time in service since over­
haul on the effective date of this AD must be  
accomplished:
(1) Within 10 hours’  time in service after  
the effective date of this AD conduct a visual  
inspection of the oil filter in accordance with  
the engine maintenance manual. If a signifi­
cant quantity of metal particles are found,  
the cause must be determined before further  
operation.
Note :  AiResearch Service Bulletin No. 624,  
dated August 28, 1970, or later FAA-approved  
revision, lists for reference the serial number  
of all new or overhauled engines which had  
less than 50 hours’  time in service since new
or overhaul on August 28, 1970, and describes  
an acceptable means of accomplishing items  
(a) and (b),
(c) Within 50 hours’  time in service after  
the effective date of this AD, revise the nor­
mal procedures section of the applicable  
FAA-Approved Airplane Flight Manuals for  
aircraft equipped with AiResearch M odel  
TPE331-1 and -2 engines tQ _  include a cau­
tionary note to read as follows:
If sudden loss or significant fluctuation of  
torque pressure indication occurs, the en­
gine should be promptly shut down and the  
cause determined before further operation.
This amendment becomes effective on  
September 22,1970.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11585 (signed 1971-03-04, 36 FR 4467) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from  this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 25333 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11585 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11585
C reating an Em ergency Board to Investigate Disputes Between Certain
Carriers Represented by the N ation al R ailw ay L abor Conference
and the Eastern, W estern, and Southeastern Carriers’ Conference
Com m ittees and C ertain of T heir Em ployees Represented by the
Brotherhood of R ailroad Signalm en
W H EREAS disputes exist between certain carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference and the Eastern, Western and 
Southeastern Carriers’ Conference Committees, designated in List A  
attached hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, a labor organi­
zation; and
W H EREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act as amended; and
W H EREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threaten substantially to interrupt commerce to a degree such as 
to deprive the country of essential transportation service:
N O W , TH E R E F O R E , by -virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from  this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and 
the Eastern, Western and Southeastern Carriers’ Conference Commit­
tees, or by their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad 
Signalmen, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11621 (signed 1971-10-04, 36 FR 19435) creates a Board of Inquiry under section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947, appoints its five members, orders a report 'on or before October 6, 1971' (a report deadline, not an end) and provides that, upon the submission of its report, the Board "shall continue in existence" to perform other functions required under the Act, so the order has no own-terms end. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by the table row at offset 25496 of the held EO_12553.txt, "11621 Creating a board of inquiry to report on labor disputes affecting the- maritime industry" (the printed hyphen after 'the' is in the held bytes), which matches this order's number and subject; the row for EO 11622, the amending order, is also in the table. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing. Held U.S. Code editorial note (22 note to 29 U.S.C. 176, release point 119-121): "Ex. Ord. No. 11621, Oct. 4, 1971, 36 F.R. 19435, as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 11622, Oct. 5, 1971, 36 F.R. 19491, which created a Board of Inquiry to inquire into issues involved in certain labor disputes, was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." The amendment by EO 11622 is a later event recorded on the clause, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert): the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends.

later_events.mechanism: amendment by EO 11622 (signed 1971-10-05, no effective-date wording; read as on signing), recorded as an event, not an end: (1) in the first paragraph, immediately after the words naming the International Longshoremen’s Association, AFL-CIO, the held FR text inserts the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, AFL-CIO and District Lodge 94 and Local Lodge 1484 thereof (before: the disputes are those of the employers and the International Longshoremen’s Association and the International Longshoremen’s and Warehousemen’s Union; after: those two unions plus the machinists’ union and its lodges); (2) in the third paragraph the name "Morris L. Myers" is deleted from the list of five Board members. The substance of the order (a Board of Inquiry on the maritime disputes) is unchanged; the amended order continues until EO 12553.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11621
Creating a Board of Inquiry To Report on Certain Labor Disputes 
Affecting the M aritime Industry of the United States
WHEREAS, there exist certain labor disputes between employers (or 
associations by which such employers are represented in collective bar­
gaining conferences) who are (1) steamship companies operating ships 
or employed as agents for ships engaged in service from or to Atlantic, 
Pacific, Great Lakes, and Gulf Coast ports of the United States, or from or 
to other ports of the United States or its territories or possessions, (2) con­
tracting stevedores, (3) contracting marine carpenters, (4) lighterage 
operators, or (5) other employers engaged in related or associated pier 
activities, and certain of their employees represented by the International 
Longshoremen’s Association, A FL-CIO , and the International Long­
shoremen’s and Warehousemen’s Union; and
WHEREAS, such disputes have resulted in strikes on Pacific, Atlantic, 
Great Lakes, and Gulf Coast ports of the United States which if permitted 
to continue will, in my opinion, affect a substantial part of the maritime 
industry, and industry engaged in trade, commerce, transportation, trans­
mission, or communication among the several States and with foreign 
nations, and will imperil the national health and safety.
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 206 of the Labor-Management Relations Act, 1947 (61 Stat. 
155; 29 U.S.G. 176), I hereby create a Board of Inquiry, consisting of:
J. Keith Mann, Chairman
Morris L. Myers
Paul Hanlon
Jacob Seidenberg
Rolf Valtin
as Members, whom Thereby appoint to inquire into the issues involved 
in such disputes.
*  The Board shall have powers and duties as set forth in Title II of such 
Act. The Board shall report to the President in accordance with the pro­
visions of Section 206 of such Act on or before October 6, 1971.
Upon the submission of its report, the Board shall continue in existence 
to perform such other functions as may be required under such Act.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11646 (signed 1972-02-08, 37 FR 2925) amends two sections of EO 11345 (Great Lakes Basin Commission): Sec. 1 inserts the Department of State among the Commission's members in Sec. 3(2) and Sec. 2 restates Sec. 5 on international coordination between the Council and the Department of State; it has no own-terms end. First end: EO 12319 (signed 1981-09-09, 46 FR 45591), which states that, in accord with a decision of the Water Resources Council, "the follow ing river b asin  com m issions sh all term inate on the date" indicated, and lists "(b) G reat Lakes B asin  Com m ission, term inated on Septem ber 30,1981." Both amended sections concern only the Commission's membership and coordination, so the clause ended when the Commission terminated, recorded as 1981-09-30. The same order then provides (Sec. 5(a)) "(a) E ffective O ctober 1, 1981, the follow ing Execu tive O rders are" revoked, listing "(2) Execu tive O rder No. 11345, as am ended, w hich establish ed  the G reat L akes" (Basin Commission): the revocation of the parent order as amended took effect on 1981-10-01, one day after the Commission's termination, and is recorded as a later event; if a reviewer reads the clause as lasting until the parent order was revoked, the first end is 1981-10-01 instead. EO 12319 does not name EO 11646 by number; the end rests on the Commission's termination and the revocation of EO 11345 'as amended'. The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 12319, September 9, 1981" (the signing date of the order whose Secs. 1 and 5 act on 1981-09-30 and 1981-10-01). Later events on the clause: EO 11882 (signed 1975-10-06) adds the Energy Research and Development Administration to Sec. 3(2) and EO 12038 (effective as of 1977-10-01 by its Sec. 6) substitutes the Department of Energy for it; both amend the same membership list, leave the Department of State insertion in place and are amendment events, not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert).

later_events.mechanism: amendment by EO 11882 Sec. 1 (signed 1975-10-06, no effective-date wording; read as on signing): Sec. 3(2) of EO 11345 is amended by adding Energy Research and Development Administration immediately after Department of Transportation; the Department of State insertion is untouched; amendment event, not an end.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
EXECUTIVE ORDER 11646
Membership of Department of State on the Great Lakes Basin 
Commission
Planning for the conservation and use of the water and related land 
resources of the Great Lakes Basin requires coordination among the 
affected State and local governments, Federal agencies, other juris­
dictions and agencies, and with the Government of Canada. To assure 
effective coordination in this regard, Executive Order No. 11345 of 
April 20, 1967, created the Great Lakes Basin Commission pursuant 
to the provisions of section 201 of the Water Resources Planning Act. 
I have now determined that the inclusion of a representative of the 
Department of State as a member of the Great Lakes Basin Commis­
sion would enhance the work of that Commission.
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 202 of the Water Resources Planning Act (79 Stat. 247; 42 
U.S.C. 1962b-l ) and as President of the United States, it is ordered as 
follows:
Sec tio n 1. Section 3(2)  of Executive Order No. 11345 of April 20, 
1967, as amended, is hereby further amended by inserting “Department 
of State,” immediately before “Department of Agriculture”.
Se c. 2. Section 5 of Executive Order No. 11345 is hereby amended 
to read as follows:
“ Se c. 5. International Coordination . The Council and the Depart­
ment of State shall consult as appropriate on matters under con­
sideration by the Commission which relate to the areas of interest and 
jurisdiction of the International Joint Commission, United States and 
Canada, and the Great Lakes Fishery Commission.”

research_rationale:
EO 11646 (signed 1972-02-08, 37 FR 2925) read in full from the held official FR text, with EO 12319, EO 11882 and EO 12038 read in the relevant parts from held FR texts. Identity confirmed. The order is a two-section amendment of EO 11345 (membership; international coordination). First end: the Great Lakes Basin Commission's termination on 1981-09-30 under EO 12319 Sec. 1(b) (decision of the Water Resources Council recited in the order), with the revocation of EO 11345 'as amended' effective 1981-10-01 (Sec. 5(a)) recorded as a later event and as the alternative first end. EO 11646 is not named by number in EO 12319; this is stated in the clause reason. The dossier's ACT leads cite the APP mirror of EO 12319; I used the held FR text. Savings: transferred_or_accrued (Sec. 3 and 4 of EO 12319 close out and transfer the commission's assets and activities to the member States). AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No instrument other than EO 12319 is shown to have ended this order's clause before 1981-09-30: the dossier chain lists EO 11882 and EO 12038 (amendments of the same membership list, later events) and EO 12319; the Cruden scan found no other held text ending or restating Sec. 3(2) or Sec. 5; current-law:usc and current-law:ecfr recorded no hit. EO 11882 and EO 12038 change other members of the same list; neither removes the Department of State.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives separately from the Commission's existence: the coordination sentence in Sec. 5 as restated binds the Council and the Department of State only 'on matters under consideration by the Commission'.","savings_check":"EO 12319 Secs. 2 to 4 direct the orderly close-out of the commissions, transfer their assets to the member States and tell Federal members to continue coordination in future State arrangements; these are consequences of the termination, not a survival of EO 11646's amendments, so the state is transferred_or_accrued with that source quoted below.","scope_check":"The dossier inventory is one whole clause covering both amended sections (Sec. 1 and Sec. 2); both concern the same Commission, are ended by the same termination, and are claimed together."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12319 (held FR text, 46 FR 45591) states in Sec. 3 that "the a sse ts o f the com m issions w hich" the Federal Government might otherwise claim are to be transferred to the member States, and Sec. 4 directs Federal members "continue coordination and cooperation in future S tate and in ter-State b asin" planning arrangements; neither continues EO 11646's amendments.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11650 (signed 1972-02-16, 37 FR 3739) orders, under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, that returns for stated taxes 'shall be open to inspection' by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establishments in accordance with Treasury Decision 6543 and its amendments. The order is a single continuing authorization. The operative words include "is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by". First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 25703 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11650 Providing for inspection of tax returns by certain persons and State and Federal establishments", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Executive Orders 10738, 10906, 10954, 10962, 11102, 11206, 11213, 11650, and 11706, listed above, were revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (26 note to 26 U.S.C. 6103)
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended (26 U.S.C. 6 1 0 3 (a)), it 
is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by 
chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 32, subchapters B and C of chapter 33, 
subchapter B of chapter 37, and chapter 41 of such Code shall be open 
to inspection by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Govern­
ment establishments in accordance and upon compliance with the rules 
and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury 
decision 6543, relating to inspection and use of returns by such classes 
of persons and State and Federal Government establishments, approved 
by the President on January 17, 1961, the amendments thereto approved 
by the President on April 4, 1963, and March 18, 1965, and the amend­
ment thereto approved by me this date.

is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by 
chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 32, subchapters B and C of chapter 33,

to inspection by certain classes of persons and State and Federal Govern­

decision 6543, relating to inspection and use of returns by such classes 
of persons and State and Federal Government establishments, approved

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11664 (signed 1972-03-31, 37 FR 6651) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report to"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 25878 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11664 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".

=== PDF page 11 of 88 ===
THE PRESIDENT 6651
E X E C U T IV E  O R D E R  11664
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between
the Penn Central Transportation Company and Certain of Its
Employees
WHEREAS, a dispute exists between the Penn Central Transporta­
tion Company and certain of its employees represented by the United 
Transportation Union, a labor organization; and
WHEREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential transporta­
tion service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I hereby create a Board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. No member of the Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or any 
carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Penn Central Transportation Company, or by its employees, in the 
conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11679 (signed 1972-08-19, 37 FR 16857) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("the dispute within thirty days from  the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from  this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 25952 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11679 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986".

EXECUTIVE ORDER 11679
C reating an Em ergency Board T o  Investigate a Dispute Between the 
Long Island R a il Road Com pany and C ertain o f Its Employees
W H E R E A S , a dispute exists between the Long Island R ail Road 
Company and certain o f its employees represented by Participating 
Labor Organizations designated in list attached hereto and made a part 
hereof; and
W H E R E A S , this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions o f the Railw ay Labor A ct, as amended; and
W H E R E A S , this dispute, in the judgment of the National M ediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive a section o f the country o f essential transpor­
tation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue o f the authority vested in me by 
section 10 o f the Railw ay Labor Act, as amended (45 U .S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate this dispute. N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily or 
otherwise interested in any organization o f railroad employees or any 
carrier.
Th e board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the dispute within thirty days from  the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 o f the Railw ay Labor A ct, as amended, 
from  this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Long Island R a il Road Company, or by its employees, in the conditions 
out o f which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11706 (signed 1973-03-08, 38 FR 6663) orders, under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, that returns for stated taxes 'shall be open to inspection' by U.S. attorneys and attorneys of the Department of Justice and for use in grand jury proceedings and in litigation in accordance with Treasury Decision 6543 and its amendments. The order is a single continuing authorization. The operative words include "hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by". First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26100 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11706 Providing for inspection of tax returns by U.S. Attorneys and justice Department attorneys for grand", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Executive Orders 10738, 10906, 10954, 10962, 11102, 11206, 11213, 11650, and 11706, listed above, were revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (26 note to 26 U.S.C. 6103)
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the In­
ternal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended (26 U.S.C. 6103(a)),  it is 
hereby ordered that returns made in respect of the taxes imposed by 
chapters 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, and 32, subchapters B and C of chapter 33, 
and chapter 41 of such Code shall be open to inspection by U.S. attorneys 
and attorneys of the Department of Justice and for use in grand jury 
proceedings and in litigation in accordance and upon compliance with 
the rules and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in 
Treasury Decision 6543, relating to inspection and use of returns by 
certain classes of persons and State and Federal Government establish­
ments, approved by the President on January 17, 1961, the amendments 
thereto approved by the President on April 4, 1963, March 18, 1965, 
and February 16, 1972, and the amendment thereto approved by me 
this date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11771 (signed 1974-03-18, 39 FR 10415) extends to the Liaison Office of the People's Republic of China in Washington, D.C. and its duly notified members the privileges and immunities of diplomatic missions, under the act of April 20, 1973 (Public Law 93-22), with the sentence "T his Executive Order shall be effective as of" followed on the next line by the date April 20, 1973. The order has no sunset or condition of its own. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26383 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11771 Extending diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". Held U.S. Code editorial note (release point 119-121): "Ex. Ord. No. 11771, Mar. 18, 1974, 39 F.R. 10415, which extended diplomatic privileges and immunities to the Liaison Office of the People’s Republic of China in Washington, D.C., was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12553, Feb. 25, 1986, 51 F.R. 7237." (22 note to 22 U.S.C. 288i)

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 11783 (signed 1974-05-21, 39 FR 18067) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act; its only commands are the board's creation, the thirty-day reporting command ("this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.") and the standstill ("from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report to"). The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts and are not ends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 report-deadline, option C); no board report is registered in this packet, so no report date is claimed. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25), whose operative sentence reads "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the table entry at offset 26648 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "11783", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25 (the Federal Register printing date, 1986-03-03, is not used). The Office of the Federal Register catalog note for this order reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 11783 is the first entry of the column and pairs by position with the first subject, "Creating an emergency- board to investigate a railroad labor dispute" (offset 27035), consistent with this order's own subject.

Title 3—The President
E X E C U T I V E  O R D E R  11783
Creating an Em ergency Board to Investigate a Dispute Between the
Carriers Represented by the N ation al R ailw ay L abor Conference
and Certain of T heir Em ployees
WHEREAS, a dispute exists between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference designated in lists attached hereto 
and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees represented by 
the Sheet Metal Workers’ International Association, a labor organization; 
and
WHEREAS, this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS, this dispute, in the judgment of the National Mediation 
Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a 
degree such as to deprive sections of the tountry of essential transporta­
tion service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a Boar cl, of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute. No member of the Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The Board shall report its finding to the President with respect to 
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report to 
the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the dispute arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Sec. 1: EO 12060 (signed 1978-05-15, 43 FR 21315) amends Sec. 1 of EO 11861 by inserting the position of Assistant Attorney General, United States Attorneys and Trial Advocacy, in level IV and substituting 'Deputy Under Secretary for Regional Affairs' in subsection (10). First end: EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18, 43 FR 37161), Sec. "1-202. Executive Order No. 11861, as amended, is hereby revoked." EO 12076 does not name EO 12060 by number; it revokes EO 11861 'as amended', and because the clause only amends EO 11861 the revocation removes the section it amends (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments is respected: the end is the instrument that names the parent as amended). EO 12076 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1978-08-18 (the FR printing date, 1978-08-22, is not used). The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 12076, August 18, 1978". Disclosed alternative reading: if a reviewer holds that an order not named by number is not ended by the revocation of its amended parent, no first end is shown in the held sources. Later events: the only later amendment held, EO 12069 (1978-06-30), changes subsection (9) of the same section and does not touch the words EO 12060 inserted, so it is not a recorded event on this clause.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12095 (signed 1978-11-02, 43 FR 51595) creates an emergency board under Section 44 of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978 to investigate the dispute between Wien Air Alaska, Inc. and certain individuals represented by the Air Line Pilots Association. The order's commands are the establishment of the board ("1-101. Establishment o f  Board.") and the thirty-day report command ("1-102. Report."). First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose preamble states that it is made "to terminate the establishing authorities for" committees that are inactive or no longer necessary and whose Sec. 5 reads "Sec. 5. Executive Order No. 12095, creating an Em ergency Board to Investigate" (the sentence continues on the next lines and ends "is revoked."). EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". The held source-ladder and family-rule texts filed under other order numbers (for example queue_EO_11022, queue_EO_11256 and queue_EO_11829) are reprints of the same 47 FR 36099 pages of EO 12379; the dossier's chain events dated 1962, 1965 and 1975 that cite them for this order come from those mislabeled files and are not events.

Title 3—The President
Executive Order 12095 November 2,1978
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate a Dispute Between Wien A ir A laska, Inc.
and Certain Individuals
A  dispute exists between Wien Air Alaska, Inc., and certain individuals  
represented by the Air Line Pilots Association, a labor organization.
Section 44 o f the Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504)  
directed that the provisions of Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended, be invoked despite the fact that the National Mediation Board has  
failed to find that the dispute in its judgment substantially threatens to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section o f the  
country o f essential transportation service.
N O W , THEREFORE, by the authority vested in me by Section 44 of the  
Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504) it is hereby ordered as  
follows:
1-101. Establishment o f  Board. There is established a board o f three mem­
bers to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of  
airline employees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with  
respect to the dispute within 30 days from the date o f this Order.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12121 (signed 1979-02-26, 44 FR 11195) amends Sec. 1-102 of EO 12083 by adding two members to the Energy Coordinating Committee, "The Director of the Community Services Administration." and "The Chairman of the Council on Wage and Price Stability."; its only command is that addition and it has no own-terms end. EO 12083 (held FR text of September 27, 1978) has no sunset: it establishes the Committee, with functions, an Executive Council and a revocation of EO 11814. First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose Sec. 20 reads "Sec. 20. Executive O rder No. 12083, as amended, establishing the Energy" (continuing on the next line: Coordinating Committee, is revoked). EO 12379 does not name EO 12121; it revokes EO 12083 'as amended', and because EO 12121's whole operative content is a textual addition to Sec. 1-102 of EO 12083, the revocation of EO 12083 as amended removes the section it amends and ends the clause (owner ruling 2026-10-21 unnamed instruments is respected: the end is the instrument that names the parent order as amended, and the reason is stated). EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". Later event: EO 12156 (signed 1979-09-10, 44 FR 53073) corrects EO 12148 Sec. 5-211 to a further amendment of Sec. 1-102 'as amended by Executive Order No. 12121' adding (z) the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency; that amendment adds a separate member and leaves the two members added by EO 12121 in place, so it is a later amendment event, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert). Disclosed alternative reading: if a reviewer holds that an order not named by number is not ended by the revocation of its amended parent, no first end is shown in the held sources.

later_events.mechanism: further amendment by EO 12156 Sec. 1-101 (signed 1979-09-10, no effective-date wording, read as on signing), recorded as an event, not an end: Sec. 1-102 of EO 12083, as amended by EO 12121, is further amended by adding in alphabetical order (z) the Director of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (before: members (x) and (y) added by EO 12121; after: the same members plus (z)); the clause continues, amended, until EO 12083 is revoked.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12159 (signed 1979-09-20, 44 FR 54687) creates an emergency board under Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the Chicago, Rock Island, Pacific Railroad & Peoria Terminal Company and two unions. The order's commands are sections 1-101 (establishment), 1-102 (report within 30 days) and 1-103 (maintaining conditions): "1-102. Report." and "from this date and for 30 days after the board has". First end: EO 12379 (signed 1982-08-17, 47 FR 36099), whose preamble states that it is made "to terminate the establishing authorities for" committees that are inactive or no longer necessary and whose Sec. 6 reads "Sec. 6. Executive O rder No. 12159, creating an Emergency Board to Investigate" (the sentence continues on the following lines and ends "is revoked."). EO 12379 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1982-08-17. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12379, August 17, 1982". The held source-ladder and family-rule texts filed under other order numbers (for example queue_EO_11022, queue_EO_11256 and queue_EO_11829) are reprints of the same 47 FR 36099 pages of EO 12379; the dossier's chain events dated 1962, 1965 and 1975 that cite them for this order come from those mislabeled files and are not events.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 12159 of September 20, 1979
Creating an Emergency Board To Investigate Disputes  
Between the Chicago, Rock Island, Pacific Railroad &  Peoria  
Terminal Company and Brotherhood of Railway, Airline &  
Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Express and Station Em­
ployees; and the United Transportation Union
Disputes exist between the Chicago, Rock Island, Pacific Railroad &  Peoria  
Terminal Company and certain of its employees represented by both the  
Brotherhood of Railway, Airline &  Steamship Clerks, Freight Handlers, Ex­
press and Station Employees; and the United Transportation Union.
These disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under the provisions of the  
Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
These disputes in the judgment of the National Mediation Board threaten  
substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a  
section of the country of essential transportation service:
N OW , TH EREFO RE, by the authority vested in me by Section 10 o f the 
R ailw ay Labor A ct, as am ended (45 U.S.C. 160), it is hereby ordered as 
follow s:
1— 101. Establishm ent o f Board. There is established a board of three members 
to be appointed by the President to investigate these disputes. No member of |  
the board shall be pecuniarily or otherw ise interested in any organization of 
railroad em ployees or any carrier.
1-102. Report. The board shall report its finding to the President with respect  
to these disputes within 30 days from the date of this Order.
* 1-103. M aintaining Conditions. A s provided by Section 10 of the R ailw ay
Labor A ct, as amended, from this date and for 30 days after the board has 
m ade its report to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be 
m ade by the Chicago, R ock Island, Pacific R ailroad &  Peoria Term inal Compa­
ny, or by its em ployees, in the conditions out of which these disputes arose.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12162 (signed 1979-09-28, 44 FR 56665) amends EO 12140 (delegation to Governors of motor gasoline end-user allocation authority) by deleting the first sentence of its Sec. 1-105; EO 12140's Sec. 1-105 began with the words "This O rder shall term inate, unless extended, at midnight on" (September 30, 1979), so the amendment removed that sunset. The amending words are "hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105." (preceded in the held text by 'Executive Order No. 12140 is'). First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26770 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "12162", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 12162 is the 21st entry of the column and pairs by position with the 21st subject, "Continuing the delegation of authorities relating to motor gasoline end-user allocation" (offset 28535), consistent with this order's subject; the parent order EO 12140 is also listed in the table (its subject precedes at the 18th position).

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of 
the United States of America, including the Emergency Petroleum Allocation 
A ct of 1973, as amended (15 U .S.C . 751 et se q .), Executive Order No. 12140 is 
hereby amended by deleting the first sentence in Sec. 1-105.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12176 (signed 1979-12-07, 44 FR 70705) revises Sections 1-401 and 1-402 of EO 12103 (President's Commission on the Coal Industry): the final report is due by March 15, 1980 (held text: "The final report required by section 1-202 of this O rder shall be" followed on the next line by the date; a report deadline, not an end) and the held FR text of Sec. 1-402 reads "shall term inate on M arch 1 5 ,1980." (the Commission shall terminate on March 15, 1980). First end: the stated sunset of Sec. 1-402 as revised, March 15, 1980, recorded inclusive (the order runs through the end of that day); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when March 15, 1980 begins, is the alternative (owner ruling 2026-10-21 until-dates). The actor is EO 12176 itself (own terms); the commission's termination ends the clause because both revised sections concern only the Commission's report and life. Later event: EO 12258 (signed 1980-12-31, 46 FR 1251), Sec. 1-103(g), revokes "Executive Order No. 12103, as amended, establishing the President’s" (continuing: Commission on the Coal Industry) in a list of orders that "that established committees which" have terminated or whose work is completed, and Sec. 1-105 provides "1-105. This Order shall be effective December 31,1980." That revocation postdates the sunset, does not name EO 12176 and is therefore a later event, not the first end. The OFR catalog note on the target reads "Revoked by: EO 12258, December 31, 1980". No extension of the March 15, 1980 date is held.

later_events.mechanism: revocation of EO 12103 'as amended' by EO 12258 Sec. 1-103(g), effective December 31, 1980 by its Sec. 1-105; a later event after the Commission's sunset, not the first end

research_rationale:
EO 12176 (signed 1979-12-07, 44 FR 70705) read in full from the held official FR text, with EO 12103 and EO 12258 read in the relevant parts. Identity confirmed. The order's only content is a revision of Secs. 1-401 and 1-402 of EO 12103: a final-report deadline (not an end) and a stated sunset of the Commission on March 15, 1980. First end: that own-terms sunset, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading stated (owner ruling 2026-10-21 until-dates); the end source is the order's own held clause text. Later event: EO 12258 Sec. 1-103(g) (effective December 31, 1980) revoking EO 12103 as amended. A Cruden scan for EO 12103 and the Commission found no other held order extending the date. The producer-registered text is the FR text; the machine sunset lead exists only for the APP mirror and is not used. Savings: none_after_bounded_search. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No instrument ended the clause before March 15, 1980: the Cruden scans for EO 12103 and for the Commission's name found only EO 12062 (an earlier order establishing a commission of the same name), EO 12103, EO 12176 and EO 12258; EO 12258 postdates the sunset. The report deadline of the same date is not an end. The dossier chain for EO 12176 lists no event; the later-events edge lists only EO 12258.","independent_command_check":"No independent command survives separately from the Commission's life: the report command and the termination are the clause's whole content.","savings_check":"No savings or residual effect is shown: EO 12258 has no savings wording for the revoked commissions and the Commission's report was due before the revocation.","scope_check":"The order has one operative paragraph revising two sections of EO 12103 (report date and sunset); both sections concern the same Commission, so the clause is treated as one whole and ends when the Commission terminates."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: EO 12189 (signed 1980-01-16, 45 FR 3559) amends EO 12153, as amended by EO 12186, to read as a restated section 1-101 to 1-104 exempting first sales of heavy crude oil from price controls under the Emergency Petroleum Allocation Act of 1973, with two definitions of 'heavy crude oil' (one for August 17 through December 20, 1979 and one from December 21, 1979 'and thereafter') and an authority for the Secretary of Energy to adopt regulations. The restated text includes the words "1-103. Effective D ecem ber 21,1 9 7 9  and thereafter," so the clause has no own-terms end; the dated window in the earlier definition ended on December 20, 1979, before the order was signed, and does not end the exemption. First end: EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25): "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" followed by a two-column 'No. Subject' table; the entry at offset 26794 of the held EO_12553.txt reads "12189", which matches this order's number and subject. EO 12553 has no effective-date wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing, 1986-02-25. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads "Revoked by: EO 12553, February 25, 1986". The held EO 12553 text prints this part of the table (PDF page 14) as a number-only column followed by a separate subject column: the number 12189 is the 25th entry and pairs with the 25th subject, "Relating to the definition of heavy oil" (offset 28862), consistent with this order's subject. An independent AI-reviewed ACT record for the same pair is carried in the dossier and agrees.

the United States of A m erica, including the Em ergency Petroleum A llocation 
A ct of 1973, as am ended (15 U.S.C. 751 e t  s e q.), and in order to provide that 
certain oil is exem pt from price controls on and after August 17,1979, and that 
other oil is exem pt on and after D ecem ber 21, 1979, it is hereby ordered that 
Executive O rder No. 12153 of August 17,1979, as am ended by Executive O rder 
No. 12186 of D ecem ber 21,1979, is am ended to read as follow s:
“1-101. Prices charged in the first sale o f heavy crude oil are exem pted from 
price controls adopted pursuant to the Em érgency Petroleum A llocation A ct o f 
1973, as amended. This exem ption shall only apply to heavy crude oil as it is 
defined, and for the time period to w hich the definition is applicable, as set 
forth in this O rder.”.
“1-102. Effective August 1 7 ,1 9 7 9  through D ecem ber 20,1979, ‘heavy crude oil’

month prior to July 1979 in w hich crude oil w as produced and sold from that

"1-104. The Secretary  of Energy may, pursuant to Executive O rder No. 11790,
